coordinates.note: Published latitude/longitude of the Handuk iron mine (the same pair appears in arXiv:1903.05368, Fig. 1), the mine in which Yemilab was built. It is the mine location, not a surveyed position of the underground halls (reached through a 782 m access tunnel from the bottom of the mine's second shaft, at about 1,000 m depth), so it is kept as a campus-grade, approximate point with a 2 km precision (an Atlas estimate).
coordinates.quote: The Handuk iron mine location (latitude: 37.188639 deg, longitude: 128.659406 deg) in Jeongseon-gun, Gangwon province, Korea, where a new underground Yemilab (∼1000 m overburden) is currently being constructed.

depth.note: Overburden at the laboratory; the AMoRE Hall floor, the deepest point, is at 1,029 m.
depth.quote: a new underground experimental facility with a depth of 1,000 m (2,500 m w. e.)

depth_mwe.note: The COSINE-100U paper (arXiv:2409.15748) gives 2,700 m w.e. for 1,000 m; the facility's own construction paper (2,500 m w.e.) is followed.
depth_mwe.quote: a new underground experimental facility with a depth of 1,000 m (2,500 m w. e.)

name: Yemilab (Handuk iron mine)
notes: The coordinate marks the Handuk mine, not the experimental halls; the hall position relative to the shaft is not published as a latitude/longitude in the papers read.
Depth figures: 1,000 m overburden everywhere; 2,500 m.w.e. (construction paper) versus 2,700 m.w.e. (COSINE-100U paper).

summary.plain: The underground halls of Yemilab, reached through a mine shaft and a long sloping tunnel at the Handuk iron mine near Jeongseon, South Korea, under about 1,000 metres of rock.
summary.technical: Experimental zone at the end of a 782 m access tunnel starting at -35 m elevation (604 m below the surface) at the bottom of the Handuk mine's 627 m second shaft; overburden ~1,000 m (AMoRE Hall floor 1,029 m, ~2,500 m.w.e.); limestone host rock; 17 dedicated experimental rooms.
